name: trie
description: A prefix tree where each path from root to a marked node spells a word. Each node has up to 26 children (for lowercase letters). Extremely efficient for prefix-based searches and autocomplete.
aim: Store a set of strings in a tree structure where each node represents a character. Common prefixes share nodes. Enables O(m) insert/search/delete where m is the key length — independent of how many strings are stored.
howItWorks: Insert: traverse from root, create nodes for missing characters
Mark end node as 'end of word'
Search: traverse matching characters from root; check end-of-word marker
Prefix search: same as search but don't require end-of-word — finds all words with a prefix
Delete: unmark end-of-word; remove dangling nodes

time.bestCase: Insert/Search on key of length m
time.averageCase: Independent of number of keys n
time.worstCase: All operations O(m) where m = key length

complexity.spaceDescription: n keys of average length m, each node has up to 26 children

realWorld: Google Search autocomplete: trie enables instant prefix matching
Spell checkers: find closest word for a misspelled prefix
IP routing tables: longest prefix matching in network routers
whenToUse: Fast prefix search across thousands of strings
alternatives: HashMap: O(m) lookup but no prefix search
Binary Search: O(m log n) but sorted array needed

beginnerAnalogy: Like a dictionary organised by letters: T-R-I-E takes you to the 'tri' shelf, then 'e' to find 'trie'. Words sharing the same prefix share the same shelf.
beginnerWhat: A tree where each level represents one letter of a word, sharing common prefixes among all stored words.
beginnerWhy: Finding all words starting with 'pre' takes O(m) time regardless of how many words are stored.
beginnerWhen: When you need fast prefix search — autocomplete, spell checking, word games.
